questions.q: What does the S3 lifecycle policy on northfield-raw-zone do?
options: Moves aging raw objects from Standard to Standard-IA at 30 days, then Glacier Instant Retrieval at 90 days
Deletes raw objects older than 30 days permanently
Moves all objects to Glacier immediately upon upload
Compresses raw CSV files into Parquet automatically
questions.explain: The lifecycle policy transitions orders/ objects to Standard-IA at day 30 and Glacier Instant Retrieval at day 90, staying instantly readable throughout.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call Redshift Serverless 'already the biggest cost lever,' even though that decision was made back in Lesson 6?
options: Because auto-pause on a bursty, month-end-heavy workload avoids paying for a 24/7 provisioned cluster, which outweighs any tuning added later
Because Redshift Serverless is free for the first year
Because the decision has nothing to do with cost, only performance
Because Lesson 6's choice will be reversed in this lesson
questions.explain: Northfield's bursty query pattern means auto-pausing Serverless billing per RPU-second beats a cluster billing 24/7 regardless of usage — an architectural decision worth more than incremental tuning.

questions.q: Why does northfield-orders-etl run only 5 G.1X workers instead of a larger worker count?
options: It's right-sized for one night's incremental partition (thanks to job bookmarks), and Glue bills per DPU-hour so over-provisioning burns budget on idle capacity
5 workers is the maximum Glue allows for any job
More workers would cause the job to fail
Worker count has no effect on Glue's billing
questions.explain: Because bookmarks limit each run to the new partition only, a small, right-sized worker count avoids paying DPU-hours for capacity the job doesn't need.

questions.q: How does querying Parquet (from Lesson 7) already function as a cost control, not just a performance one?
options: Athena bills per byte scanned, and Parquet's columnar format routinely cuts bytes scanned by 70-90% versus raw CSV for the same query
Parquet files are free to store regardless of size
Parquet eliminates the need for an Athena workgroup entirely
It has no cost implication, only faster query results
questions.explain: Since Athena's billing unit is bytes scanned, Parquet's column pruning directly reduces cost, not just latency.

questions.q: Why does the lifecycle policy keep raw objects in S3 Standard for the first 30 days instead of tiering them immediately?
options: That's the window a re-run or backfill might realistically need to access the data quickly
S3 Standard is required for the first 30 days by AWS policy
Standard-IA cannot store CSV files
It has no reason — 30 days was picked at random
questions.explain: The guide explains the 0-30 day window in Standard covers the period a re-run or backfill might still need the raw object readily available.
